subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: When a native Codex approval relay is unavailable before invocation, may execution fall back to generic before-tool policy, or must OpenClaw restore the native relay before continuing?
rationale: The choice determines which enforcement path owns native tool approval after a transport failure, and repository history deliberately preserves fail-closed behavior for unknown unavailable states.

options.title: Restore native enforcement
options.body: Regenerate or refresh the relay descriptor and keep unknown failures fail-closed until the native approval path is restored.

options.title: Approve equivalent fallback
options.body: Permit generic policy fallback only after live proof demonstrates equivalent denials, prompts, and policy coverage.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Retain current behavior until the lifecycle can recover without changing the approval boundary.

recommendation.title: Restore native enforcement
recommendation.body: Regenerate or refresh the relay descriptor and keep unknown failures fail-closed until the native approval path is restored.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest decision history is the merged guarded fallback contract and direct inspection of the relevant Codex hook behavior.
